title: Igorota potato (BSU Po3): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Igorota potato: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: Igorota potato is a potato variety. 100 to 120 days to harvest, 23.7 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits. Compare it with others.
excerpt: Igorota is a registered potato variety, also sold or known as BSU Po3 or Igorota (BSU Po3). It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 1997 as NSIC 1997 Po 04. It takes 100 to 120 days from planting to harvest, with 23.7 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

**Yield:** 23.7 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.caption: Key facts of Igorota
rows: BSU Po3, Igorota (BSU Po3), NSIC Po 04

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Igorota potato takes 100 to 120 days from planting to harvest. That is 6.5 days longer than the average of the 11 potato varieties with a day count, 103.5 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 23.7 t/ha beats the average of its group, 21.79. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing. Its seller gives 100 to 120 days.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting. Read up on [late blight](/diseases/late-blight).

The pests and diseases that hit potato fields most often: [early blight](/diseases/early-blight), [bacterial soft rot](/diseases/soft-rot), [bacterial wilt](/diseases/bacterial-wilt), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm), [leafminer](/pests/leafminer). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Its roots have pale yellow flesh and yellow skin. Dry matter is 18.21 percent. A higher dry matter cooks mealy and gives processors more flour or starch from each tonne.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** 23.7 t/ha in registry trials, 21.61 t/ha in BSU chip trials.
**Fruit:** Pale yellow flesh, yellow skin, round to round oval tubers, shallow eyes, dry matter about 18 percent.
Resistant to late blight and peach scale insect.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: one of the three potatoes Benguet and Mountain Province farmers prefer most, and the processing check in BSU chip trials. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Igorota potato

It suits highland areas. Potato grows in the cool highlands of Benguet, Mountain Province and Bukidnon. Plant clean seed tubers, and pick a variety rated against late blight for the wet season. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for root crops](/land-preparation/root-crop-land-preparation).

items.q: Is BSU Po3 the same as Igorota?
items.a: Yes. BSU Po3 is another name for Igorota, registered as NSIC 1997 Po 04. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes 100 to 120 days from planting to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 23.7 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Igorota?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
